items.title: Manny Albam interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: They were dealing with great players. Jerome Richardson.

ctx.x: Really. After working with the guys on these things.

Some of the guys would come in and be in the horn section. You’d have like Marvin Stamm or Bill Watrous or whatever. They’d just come in, sit down and go [scats] and leave, and pick up their 90 dollars or whatever. And the groups didn’t know then who they were dealing with yet. They were dealing with great players. Jerome Richardson. These guys were — they had no idea. So God bless them. My kids love the Beatles. You know you can’t do anything about that. I like them, especially towards the end when they started…
